title: Case Study Metrics + Proof Guide (Worksheet Template)
content:
Purpose
- Single source of truth for performance/cost/reliability metrics used in public case studies and sales enablement assets.
- Prevents “orphan metrics” (numbers without method, timeframe, or approval trail).
- Aligns with Product Marketing proof requirements and Legal consent boundaries.

How to use this sheet
1) Create one row per customer + workload (some customers will have multiple workloads; split them).
2) Fill Baseline and After Redwood with the same measurement method + timeframe whenever possible.
3) If exact numbers cannot be published, capture exact internally and publish ranges externally (note both).
4) Do not draft final case study copy until the “Publish OK?” column is Yes.

Definitions (use consistently)
- p95 latency (ms): end-to-end request latency at the API boundary (client send -> full response received) OR server-side (gateway receive -> response). Specify which in “Measurement notes.”
- TTFT (ms): time to first token for streaming responses (if applicable). Specify model + prompt shape.
- Throughput (tok/s): tokens generated per second (server-side) OR effective tok/s per request (client-side). Specify.
- Uptime (%): availability over a stated window for the relevant endpoint/model/deployment (Hosted/Dedicated/Private). Use Redwood status/Console for Redwood-side, customer monitoring for client-side.
- $/1M tokens: (total inference cost in period / total tokens in period) * 1,000,000. Specify whether “total tokens” = input+output or output-only.
- Window: measurement period (e.g., “14 days post-cutover,” “Oct 1–Oct 14, 2025”). Avoid single-day snapshots unless explicitly called out.

Confidence scale
- High: measured from primary source + reproducible query/dashboard + validated by Solutions Eng.
- Medium: measured but partial coverage OR mixed sources OR caveats (e.g., only peak hours).
- Low: estimate/derived from back-of-envelope or customer anecdote. Do not publish Low.

Approval statuses (public-facing)
- Internal (PMM/SE) approved: claim language + math checks complete.
- Customer approved: customer champion approved the metric statement (email/Doc comment OK).
- Legal approved: logo/quote/metric disclosure rights confirmed per consent form.
- Publish OK: all three above are complete AND any open support incidents that could materially contradict the metric are resolved/footnoted.

Hard rules
- Always include: model name + version (or family), deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), and workload shape (context length range + output length range) somewhere in proof notes.
- Never publish: customer spend in $ (unless explicitly approved), absolute token volumes (unless approved), or competitor names in comparative claims.
- If metric is an improvement claim (%), store the underlying before/after values internally.

Metric phrasing guidelines (public copy)
- Prefer: “Reduced p95 latency by ~30–40%” over “Reduced p95 latency by 37.2%.”
- Prefer: “Achieved 99.9%+ availability on Dedicated endpoints (rolling 30 days)” over “99.93%” unless explicitly approved.
- If using ranges, ensure ranges are true and not marketing-inflated; note exact internally.

Worksheet columns (copy/paste template)
Columns:
A. Customer
B. Workload / endpoint (e.g., chat assistant, embeddings, rerank, summarization)
C. Deployment mode (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
D. Model (before)
E. Model (after)
F. Baseline timeframe
G. After Redwood timeframe
H. Baseline measurement method (Console, customer APM, load test, provider invoice, etc.)
I. After measurement method
J. p95 latency baseline (ms)
K. p95 latency after (ms)
L. p95 latency public statement (exact or range)
M. TTFT baseline (ms)
N. TTFT after (ms)
O. TTFT public statement
P. Throughput baseline (tok/s)
Q. Throughput after (tok/s)
R. Throughput public statement
S. Uptime baseline (%)
T. Uptime after (%)
U. Uptime public statement
V. $/1M tokens baseline (input+output or specify)
W. $/1M tokens after
X. Cost public statement
Y. Notes on workload shape (context/output lengths, concurrency)
Z. Proof artifact link(s) (dashboard screenshot link, query, report, invoice excerpt)
AA. Confidence (High/Medium/Low)
AB. Internal owner (who can reproduce)
AC. SE validation (Yes/No; name + date)
AD. PMM validation (Yes/No; name + date)
AE. Customer approval (Yes/No; who + date)
AF. Legal approval (Yes/No; who + date)
AG. Publish OK? (Yes/No)
AH. Notes / caveats (including exclusions and known incidents)

Template rows (blank)
Row 2 (blank template):
Customer | Workload | Mode | Model before | Model after | Baseline window | After window | Baseline method | After method | p95 base | p95 after | p95 public | TTFT base | TTFT after | TTFT public | Thru base | Thru after | Thru public | Uptime base | Uptime after | Uptime public | $/1M base | $/1M after | $/1M public | Shape notes | Proof links | Confidence | Internal owner | SE validation | PMM validation | Customer approval | Legal approval | Publish OK | Caveats

Example rows (for format only; replace with verified values before any publication)
1) Northwind Commerce | Ecommerce search + chat assistant | Dedicated | (prior provider) | (Redwood-verified open model) | 2 wks pre-cutover | 2 wks post-cutover | Customer APM + provider dashboards | Redwood Console + customer APM | [exact] | [exact] | “~30–40% lower p95 latency” | [exact] | [exact] | “Improved TTFT by ~20–30%” | [exact] | [exact] | “Higher sustained throughput under peak load” | [exact] | [exact] | “99.9%+ availability (rolling 30 days)” | [exact] | [exact] | “~15–25% lower $/1M tokens” | Context: 4–8k; Output: 200–800; concurrency: peak hours | Link to Grafana/Console export + query ID | Medium/High | Markus Klein | Yes (name/date) | Yes (name/date) | Pending | Pending | No | Note any incident windows excluded

2) Helios Health | Regulated summarization + RAG | Private (VPC) | Self-hosted | Redwood Private | Month pre-migration | Month post-migration | Load test + internal monitoring | Load test + internal monitoring | [exact] | [exact] | “Met p95 < X ms target” (or range) | [n/a] | [n/a] | “Streaming enabled for clinician UX” | [exact] | [exact] | “Improved throughput at same hardware budget” | [exact] | [exact] | “Operational reliability with audit logging + KMS” (avoid % unless approved) | [exact] | [exact] | “Reduced infra cost per request” (avoid tokens if blocked) | Context/output ranges; PHI-safe notes | Link to test report + anonymized dashboard | Medium | Simran Kaur | Yes | Yes | Pending | Pending | No | Use compliance-safe language; anonymize where required

3) Polaris DevTools | Developer copilot | Hosted API | N/A | Redwood Hosted | Prior month | Current month | Invoice-based estimate | Redwood usage analytics | [exact] | [exact] | “Shipped in <2 weeks; improved latency by ~X%” | [exact] | [exact] | “Faster first token via streaming” | [exact] | [exact] | “Handled traffic spikes without re-architecting” | [n/a] | [exact] | “Reliability supported launch week” | [exact] | [exact] | “Lower unit cost with batching/caching recommendations” | Prompt shapes vary; note P50/P95 mix | Console usage report link | Medium | Tyler Benson | Yes | Yes | Pending | Pending | No | Avoid overstating if workload varies widely

Proof artifacts (acceptable)
- Redwood Console export (token/cost/latency breakdown) with filters saved and shared internally.
- Customer APM screenshot/export with query + timeframe.
- Load test report (k6/locust) including configuration and summary tables.
- Incident report excerpt if reliability claims are made.
- For cost: invoice excerpt or usage report + calculation notes. If customer won’t share spend, publish only relative change or range.

Disclaimers (copy-ready)
- “Results are based on a production workload over [time window] and may vary by model, prompt shape, and traffic patterns.”
- “Latency measured as p95 at the API boundary over the stated window.” (Adjust if server-side.)
- “Cost per 1M tokens includes input and output tokens unless otherwise specified.”

Common failure modes (avoid)
- Mixing baseline client-side latency with after server-side latency.
- Publishing percent improvements without retaining the source numbers and method.
- Using peak-day improvements as representative without stating seasonality.
- Referencing model changes without stating that the model changed (attribution risk).

Operational checklist (before publishing a metric)
- SE validation complete (Markus/Simran or delegate) + date logged.
- PMM validation complete (Soojin) + claim language matches messaging pillars.
- Legal approval logged (Michael/Sofia) + consent scope covers metrics disclosure.
- CSM/AE confirm customer is comfortable with cadence and any reference-call load.
- If there was a recent Sev-1/Sev-2 incident affecting the customer, add caveat or choose different window.

Owner notes / TODO
- TODO: Add a single standardized “Measurement boundary” dropdown (client vs server) to reduce ambiguity.
- TODO: Confirm RevOps tagging for “reference used” deals; link once finalized.
